The algorithm adaptively extracts the overlapping point clouds by identifying the correct matching results and constructs an optimized ICP alignment. By controlling the radius range of the point cloud search, our method allows for quick extrinsic calibration of two LiDARs with low-overlap FoV. Experiments show that our algorithm achieves a more robust and accurate low-overlap registration than other methods, and also has speed advantages in general situations.

articleTitle: Rethink Object Tracking Based on Transformer
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on High Performance Big Data and Intelligent Systems (HDIS)
abstract: Most visual tracking networks with transformers use attention mechanisms instead of convolutional structures. Few new methods have focused on comparing objects and search regions in visual tracking networks. However, the association information between the target in the first frame and the search area in subsequent frames will significantly affect the predicted results of subsequent targets. As a result, we propose a tracking structure: TEDTrack, which makes full use of the correlation between a given target and the search area of the following image. TED (transformer encoder-decoder, TED) is a feature fusion mechanism of TEDTrack, which mainly uses a transformer codec to integrate the extracted template features and the next frame search region features. It can achieve better results than the Previous single-target tracking algorithm which adopted the Siamese network. The tracker in this paper has conducted many experiments on multiple challenging short-term and long-term benchmark datasets. The experimental results show the effectiveness of TEDTrack.

articleTitle: Ontology-Based APT Attack Detection and Defense Countermeasures
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on High Performance Big Data and Intelligent Systems (HDIS)
abstract: Cyberspace security has risen to the height of national strategies, represented by APT attacks, threatening important industries in various countries. In order to ensure cyberspace security, it is urgent to develop situational awareness of APT attacks. In view of the multi-step attack characteristics of APT, this paper proposes a series of questions that need to be answered in cyberspace threat situational awareness, and constructs the APT attack ontology. And through the representation and reasoning of a case, the consistency and effectiveness of the APT attack ontology are verified. It is proved that the ontology can realize the automatic correlation and reasoning of APT attack multi-source intelligence, find the weaknesses and loopholes exploited by each step of the attack, and deduce the corresponding mitigation measures. At the same time, we will find the causal relationship between various weaknesses and mitigation measures, and provide support for the auxiliary decision-making of country's cyberspace asset protection.

articleTitle: Supervisory Event Loop-based Autoscaling of Node.js Deployments
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on High Performance Big Data and Intelligent Systems (HDIS)
abstract: Autoscaling mechanisms are used widely to scale computing instances, under varying load conditions. Containerized cloud applications managed by orchestrators-such as Kubernetes with the Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA)-can be scaled based on CPU utilization. However, the prevalent approach may not be ideal for every language runtime, such as the event-driven Node.js. Language runtime-specific metrics can be utilized to accurately describe the state of the application and use it to monitor and affect the application scalability in control loop-based systems at the desired conditions dynamically. Hence, we investigate event loop lag as an alternative and Node.js-specific metric to drive autoscaling with HPA controllers. Additionally, we synthesize a three-tier adaptive mechanism on top of the cluster autoscaler, which acts as a supervisory controller, to change the setpoint value dynamically based on the divergence from the service level objectives. We further extend the aforementioned architecture to re-evaluate the system model and the controller gain parameters at runtime. To assess the methodology, we evaluate and compare the performance of our adaptive autoscaling approach against the CPU-utilization-based autoscaling mechanism, under various load patterns and workloads.
